transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (ElmBridge Head of Platform), Ravi Kapoor (ElmBridge Security Architect), Sofia Alvarez (ElmBridge DevOps), Ethan Park (ElmBridge Product)

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Okay everyone welcome, thanks for carving time. this is Alex from Redwood inference, joining with Priya and Diego on the technical side. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya Chen: doing well thanks, Maya here. we run the inference platform for ElmBridge, looking to replace our homegrown thing with something with better cost characteristics and SLA.
[00:16] Ravi Kapoor: hi all, Ravi. main reason I'm on is security posture - keys, retention, auditability, S-S-O SAML integration.
[00:22] Priya Shah: great, that's exactly what we wanted to zero in on today. quick agenda: clarify your constraints (keys, logs, identity), tradeoffs across hosted/dedicated/private, and outline next steps. sound good?
[00:31] Sofia Alvarez: yep sounds good. we'll probably ask about network egress, VPC peering, and also whether Redwood keeps any customer PII on the control plane.
[00:40] Alex Morgan: excellent. quick note on timelines — we heard you wanted a pilot in Q3, is that still the target?
[00:45] Ethan Park: yes ideally early september pilot, but security gating will determine that.

[03:02] Priya Shah: first question on keys — do you require customer-managed keys for all workloads or just for sensitive models?
[03:10] Ravi Kapoor: we need customer-managed KMS for any production model that touches PII or financial data. for evals it's okay to use provider-managed keys but we prefer consistent policies. also if there's an HSM-backed requirement we need to know where the keys live.
[03:27] Diego Ruiz: in Redwood Hosted we offer BYOK via customer-managed keys with integrations into AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault; we also support HSM-backed key wrapping for Dedicated/Private in certain contracts. note: for Hosted there's a control plane fingerprint exchange but the cryptographic material stays in your KMS, we only get sealed tokens for routing.
[03:50] Ravi Kapoor: when you say 'we only get sealed tokens' — can you clarify what metadata Redwood sees and what is considered PII?
[03:58] Priya Shah: yes. by default the control plane sees request headers, usage metrics, and non-sensitive model telemetry. customers can opt into minimal telemetry for Dedicated/private. payloads are not stored in plaintext by Redwood; we can configure retention to zero for request bodies in Private deployments. small caveat: some transient logging for debugging might be present until you opt into stricter retention.

[06:20] Maya Chen: SOC2 and ISO — do you have artifacts we can share with our auditors?
[06:27] Alex Morgan: yes, we can share SOC 2 Type II attestation and the Redwood security whitepaper. I'll attach network diagrams and the control plane architecture.
[06:34] Ethan Park: do you have a gap assessment for ISO 27001, or is SOC2 your primary audit?
[06:40] Priya Shah: SOC2 is currently our primary attestation for hosted customers. we have an ISO mapping document that highlights controls that align, but full ISO certification is on the roadmap.

[08:05] Ravi Kapoor: SSO — our enterprise uses Okta, we need SAML + SCIM for group provisioning. can you map SAML groups to RBAC roles?
[08:13] Diego Ruiz: yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for group sync. you can map SAML assertion attributes to RBAC roles in the console. small note - group sync latency can be up to a minute depending on your IdP.
[08:28] Sofia Alvarez: what about just-in-time (JIT) provisioning?
[08:31] Priya Shah: supported, you can use JIT for short-lived access. also we support enforcing MFA via your IdP.

[11:00] Maya Chen: audit logs — retention policy, access controls, and ability to push logs to our SIEM?
[11:07] Alex Morgan: audit logs are configurable. Hosted customers get default 90-day retention with export to S3 or a syslog endpoint; Dedicated customers can configure longer retention or push logs to your own SIEM via fluentd or secure forwarding. for Private, logs stay in your environment and Redwood does not ship copies unless configured.
[11:29] Ravi Kapoor: who has access to audit logs inside Redwood?
[11:33] Priya Shah: access is role-based. only designated security/ops roles from Redwood can access logs for support and only with customer approval; everything is logged and requestable via the audit trail. we'll share the access matrix in the follow-up.

[13:45] Ethan Park: data residency — we need EU-only processing for a subset of customers. can you pin the inference to region?
[13:52] Diego Ruiz: yes, we can route requests to regional clusters. Hosted supports region selection for model serving; Dedicated gives you a regional pool in a specific cloud region; Private you fully control locality. important to note: if you use control-plane features that live in a different region, telemetry might cross borders unless you deploy Private control plane.

[16:10] Ravi Kapoor: encryption at rest — are model artifacts encrypted and who holds the keys?
[16:16] Priya Shah: model artifacts are encrypted at rest in all deployments. key ownership depends: Hosted can use provider-managed keys or customer-managed KMS (BYOK). Dedicated can be configured with customer KMS and HSM wrapping. Private is fully customer-controlled.

[19:05] Maya Chen: network connectivity — can we do VPC peering or private link?
[19:12] Diego Ruiz: yes, Hosted supports AWS PrivateLink and GCP VPC peering for certain regions. Dedicated supports VPC peering and can provide static egress IPs. Private of course runs in your network. there are some egress rules for model downloads and updates but those can be whitelisted.

[22:40] Ravi Kapoor: how about model version rollouts — do you capture differences in output for regressions and do you keep diffs in the audit?
[22:48] Priya Shah: Redwood Optimize includes rollout tooling and qualitative/eval metrics; you can tie evals to rollouts and we can archive a snapshot of prompts and outputs for an audit window. we store hashes of outputs for integrity and can provide redaction tooling if needed.

[26:00] Maya Chen: legal will want to know about data retention and deletion guarantees for contracts. do you give contractual SLAs for data deletion?
[26:08] Alex Morgan: yes we offer contractual data deletion commitments for Dedicated and Private customers. for Hosted we have documented retention windows and can provide custom terms on enterprise contracts. deletion workflows include WORM retention exceptions and verifiable deletion logs.

[29:30] Sofia Alvarez: onboarding and support — what level of access do we get to logs and metrics?
[29:36] Diego Ruiz: you'll get tenant-level dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route tracing. for Dedicated there is deeper host-level telemetry. Support runs in tiers; enterprise customers get a named CSM and 24/7 on-call for severity 1 incidents.

[33:20] Ravi Kapoor: two other items — do you support customer-supplied model images (OCI) and can we sign them into your runtime?
[33:28] Priya Shah: yes for Dedicated and Private you can bring custom model artifacts and images; we have a signing and verification process. Hosted supports curated public models, but we can host privately-scoped versions in Dedicated/Private.

[36:10] Ethan Park: curious about where backups live and what encryption covers — snapshots of KV cache, model weights, etc?
[36:17] Diego Ruiz: snapshots are encrypted; KV cache is ephemeral and not backed up by default. model weights and checkpoints are backed up and encrypted at rest. backup keys follow the same KMS policy as artifacts.

[39:45] Maya Chen: for pilot sizing — we expect 150 qps peak for inference with p50 latency under 200ms. what deployment would you recommend?
[39:53] Priya Shah: for that latency and throughput Dedicated is often the sweet spot — reserved capacity to ensure p50 < 200ms with autoscaling headroom. if you need strict key control and on-prem locality, Private. we can run a performance baseline during the pilot.

[42:01] Ravi Kapoor: final clarifying question — control plane telemetry, are IP addresses or user identifiers stored?
[42:07] Alex Morgan: control plane stores IPs for security logs, but they can be redacted; user identifiers are minimal and you can opt out of PII collection for Dedicated/Private. we'll note that in the follow-up.

[44:50] Alex Morgan: great wrap — quick recap and next steps: I'll send SOC2, architecture diagram, and the security brief; Priya will set the tech deep-dive; Maya will send retention / data classification snippet; Ravi will provide KMS/HSM requirements. any other items?
[45:10] Maya Chen: nope that's it. thanks everyone.
[45:15] Ethan Park: thanks team.
[46:00] Alex Morgan: we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. talk soon.

End of transcript.
